kind: standing rule: registered text versus implementation conformance

why_it_exists.statement: DC-005 was found ONLY because it produced an anomalous result. Had that unregistered stricter rule happened to produce a plausible-looking result, it would never have been found.
why_it_exists.assessment_verbatim: This is a heavier problem than DC-005 itself.
why_it_exists.the_general_fault: a divergence between what a criterion says and what the code does is invisible whenever the divergence happens to be flattering, or merely unremarkable

the_rule.statement: Before any pre-registered criterion is applied to data, a line-by-line conformance table of REGISTERED TEXT against IMPLEMENTED BEHAVIOUR must be produced and committed.
the_rule.enforcement: if the conformance table is not committed, or does not pass, the criterion may not run
the_rule.scope: every registered criterion, not only new ones
the_rule.retroactive_requirement: a conformance pass over all existing OD entries is the first step of R-1b

the_directionality_criterion.rule: Changing the IMPLEMENTATION to match the REGISTERED TEXT is a bug fix. Changing the REGISTERED TEXT to match the DATA is p-hacking.
the_directionality_criterion.how_it_resolved_DC_005: the correction moved the implementation back toward the registered text, so it was a bug fix rather than a choice of the more convenient reading
the_directionality_criterion.the_supporting_check_that_made_it_verifi: the negative control was clean under BOTH readings, so the correction could not have been rescuing it

what_a_conformance_entry_must_contain: a plain statement of what the code actually does
a verdict: CONFORMS, or DIVERGES with the divergence described
for numeric constants, the registered value and the value in code, compared
claim_ceiling: A governance rule. It licenses no claim of any kind.
